git-log docs, `[--] <path>...`: "Show only commits that are enough to explain how the files that match the specified paths came to be. See History Simplification below for details and other simplification modes." History Simplification, Default mode: "Simplifies the history to the simplest history explaining the final state of the tree." DESCRIPTION: "Shows the commit logs." Both halves of the claim, including "simplified by default, not every change that ever touched the file", are supported.

claim_verdicts.source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-blame (version-current page; git pinned at 2.46 in versions.yaml)

issues.quote: A change is safe when you know what reaches the line you touch and what that line feeds.
issues.text: Unlisted claim: no entry in the ledger covers it (15 and 16 are about reading order and about history; neither defines safety). It is stated as a sufficient condition — "is safe when" — and knowing a line's callers and callees is not sufficient: the same value may be written in a second place (the lesson's own §5 finds the price twice, in db/seed.sql:7 and CollectionsChoice.cs:13), and nothing here covers tests, data already stored, or concurrent writers. Quiz q3 key (c) and q6 key (a) both rest on this sentence.
issues.fix: Weaken to a necessary condition and add it to `claims` as kind `opinion`: "You cannot judge a change until you know what reaches the line you touch and what that line feeds — and that is what one path gives you, without the rest of the repository." Then check q3 option c and q6 option a still read as the lesson's words.

issues.quote: Eight folders sit at the top: `db`, `docs`, `git-playground`, `lab`, `outputs`, `samples`, `scripts`, `www`.
issues.text: True of a copy taken straight from the repository only. Try it step 1 tells the reader to run `scripts/up.sh`, which runs `./scripts/dev-secrets.sh` (up.sh:6), whose line 6 is `mkdir -p secrets` — after that the top level has nine folders, the ninth being `secrets` (ignored by .gitignore:2, which is why it is not in the tag). A reader who starts the lab before running `ls` counts nine and cannot reconcile it with the lesson or with quiz q2, which repeats "eight folder names".
issues.fix: Write "Eight folders sit at the top of a fresh copy: …" and, in the paragraph in §4 that accounts for the other three names, add that starting the lab adds a ninth, `secrets`, which is not part of the repository. Quiz q2's stem can stay as it is once §2 says "a fresh copy".

issues.quote: One script walks list steps 1, 2 and 4, each a single command
issues.text: The script's fourth step is not a single command: map-codebase.sh:22 is `grep -rn 'Chuột không dây' db samples | head -3`, two programs joined by a pipe — exactly the construction the prereq [[foundation.l1.pipes-and-filters]] teaches as two commands. The same overstatement returns later in "Its search settles the situation in one command" and in §7's "Both answers took one command".
issues.fix: Say "each one line" instead of "each a single command", "Its search settles the situation in one line" instead of "in one command", and "Both answers took one line" in §7 — or keep "one command" only for the reader's own `grep -rn 'Bàn phím cơ' db samples`, which really is one.

issues.quote: When it is assembled from pieces or read from the database, search for a stable fragment instead.
issues.text: Contradicted two paragraphs later by the lesson's own demonstration. `Chuột không dây` is a database row — it is served from the products table at run time — and searching for the whole string still lands on it in one step, because db/seed.sql:7 writes it out literally. As written, a reader who sees a product name on screen is told not to search for the whole string, and then watches the whole string work.
issues.fix: Add the condition: "When it is assembled from pieces, search for a stable fragment instead. Rows from the database are found only when some file in the repository writes them out too, as `db/seed.sql` does here." Align claim 17 in .meta.json with the same wording.

issues.quote: `scripts/up.sh` for the lab, the small Linux machine this repository's lesson scripts run inside
issues.text: Over-general by one script. 30 of the 31 scripts under `scripts/<folder>/` begin with `[ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec "$(dirname "$0")/../lab-run.sh" "$0" "$@"`, which is what puts them in the lab; `scripts/debug/run-throws-deep.sh` has no such line — it does `cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."` then `dotnet run --project samples/DonHang.Samples`, on the host. Claim 13 carries the same overstatement from the other side (its list of host-side scripts omits that file and scripts/capture-output.sh).
issues.fix: Write "the small Linux machine nearly every one of this repository's lesson scripts re-runs itself inside", and correct claim 13's list in .meta.json to include scripts/capture-output.sh and scripts/debug/run-throws-deep.sh among the scripts that run outside the lab.

issues.quote: In that same folder on your own machine, run `grep -rn 'Bàn phím cơ' db samples`; this search only reads files, so it needs no lab.
issues.text: "Needs no lab" is true; "on your own machine" is not always runnable. Every other command the reader is given runs inside the lab box precisely so the result is the same on Windows, macOS and Linux (lab/Dockerfile; the /.dockerenv re-exec line). A Windows reader has no `grep` in the default shell, and the pattern is non-ASCII. The step promises two specific lines that only a POSIX shell will produce.
issues.fix: Name the shell that works either way: "In that same folder, run `grep -rn 'Bàn phím cơ' db samples` — in a shell that has `grep` (Git Bash, WSL, macOS or Linux Terminal), or inside the lab with `ssh -p 2222 -i secrets/lab_key dev@localhost` and `cd /repo`. The search only reads files, so the lab is not required for it."

issues.quote: `grep -rn` for a string written out literally in the code is the shortest route from a behaviour to the line that produced it.
issues.text: "The shortest route" is a superlative the lesson never establishes and cannot: a stack trace, a debugger or a log line can name the file and line just as directly, and none of those is compared here. §4's own wording is the defensible one — "that lands you on the line in one step". The superlative comes from the example repo's Vietnamese prose ("con đường ngắn nhất … và luôn dùng được"), which the lesson quotes but does not have to assert in its own voice.
issues.fix: Rewrite summary line 3 as: "When a string you saw is written out literally in the code, `grep -rn` lands you on the line that produced it in one step, without reading anything first."

issues.quote: Actually reading with no question does not stick: you have nothing to hang the detail on.
issues.text: Stated as a fact about how reading works, with no condition and no source; claim 15 is hedged ("yields usable understanding faster than reading files in order") and the lesson's sentence is not. No document in versions.yaml or under refs/ governs it, so "does not stick" cannot be supported as written. Quiz q3's explanation for option b repeats it ("the detail has nothing to hang on and does not stick").
issues.fix: Restore the hedge: "Actually reading with no question in hand pays off slowly: there is less to hang the detail on." Use the same softened wording in the q3 option-b explanation.

issues.quote: In that same folder on your own machine, run `grep -rn 'Bàn phím cơ' db samples`; this search only reads files, so it needs no lab.
issues.text: "On your own machine" tells me step 2 was somewhere else, but step 2 says nothing about where I type it, and Core concepts says the lesson scripts run inside the lab. I would stop at step 2 rather than risk typing it in the wrong place.

issues.quote: From the top folder of the example repository, run `scripts/up.sh` and wait for it to finish — that starts the lab.
issues.text: Nothing tells me how long this wait is or what it needs on my machine, and the lesson budgets three minutes for all three steps. If it runs long I cannot tell whether it is working or stuck. Step 3 says its search needs no lab, which makes me wonder whether step 2 really needs it either.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence on what the end looks like and why it is needed: "…and wait for it to finish — that starts the lab, which the script runs inside; you are back at your prompt when it is up."

issues.quote: intent and reason — the two questions code will not answer about itself: what it should do, which the tests state
issues.text: "Tests" carries two of the diagram's seven boxes and two quiz options, but it is never said what a test is. §4 adds "A test states what the code should do, in a form you can run", which tells me what it is for, not what it is. I could answer q5 option e only by trusting that sentence, not by knowing what I would be opening in `samples/DonHang.Samples.Tests`.
issues.fix: Extend the Core concepts line at its first use: "what it should do, which the tests state — small programs that run the code with known input and check the answer".

issues.quote: search for a stable fragment instead
issues.text: "A stable fragment" is never shown. I do not know how much of a string counts as a fragment, or what makes one stable, so if the whole-string search fails I have no second move. The Try it exercise only uses a whole string, so I never practise it either.
issues.fix: Add four words of example after "stable fragment": "— the part that is not the changing bit, `không dây` rather than the whole label".

issues.quote: The other three — `git-playground`, `lab` and `outputs` — say nothing about a price, and a name you cannot read is not a reason to open the folder.
issues.text: One section earlier I was told what the lab is (the small Linux machine the scripts run inside), so `lab` is a name I can read, and I stopped to check whether I had misunderstood one of the two places. The sentence only needs the names to be irrelevant to a price, not unreadable.
issues.fix: Replace "and a name you cannot read is not a reason to open the folder" with "and a name that says nothing about your question is not a reason to open the folder".
